ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a circle, with the center labeled O. A is at the left end of the circle, B is at the right end of the circle, and AB is a horizontal diameter passing through O. C is at the upper left of the circle, D is at the lower left of the circle, and the figure shows chord AC, chord CD, and radius OD. What is required is the central angle ∠BOD. Reasoning: It is known that ∠ACD = 35°; it is an inscribed angle, and the arc it subtends is AD. The central angle corresponding to the same arc AD is ∠AOD, so ∠AOD = 2∠ACD = 2 × 35° = 70°. Because AB is a diameter, A, O, and B are collinear, and ∠AOB = 180°. Therefore ∠BOD = 180° − ∠AOD = 180° − 70° = 110°.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: A and B are opposite endpoints of a horizontal diameter through center O; C and D lie on the circle on the left side, with chords CA and CD drawn, and segment OD drawn so that ∠BOD is the central angle to find. From the text, use that ∠ACD = 35° and AB is a diameter of circle O. Since ∠ACD is an inscribed angle subtending arc AD, the corresponding central angle ∠AOD is twice it: ∠AOD = 70°. Because A, O, B are collinear on the diameter, ∠AOB = 180°, so ∠BOD = 180° − ∠AOD = 110°.
